# @whoisddd/dsh-approval-notify
English | 中文
A minimal browser-only DSH Web GUI plugin that reminds you when a session needs attention or a backg
round session finishes.
Version 0.2.1 targets DSH **0.2.1-alpha.1**. It reads labels from `sessions.list` and attention stat
e from the public `uiSession.sessionStatus` observable: `pendingInteraction` for approval/question/p
lan review and `completionUnread` for background completion. It prefers native browser notifications
, and falls back to a larger stacked toast panel when native notifications are unavailable. On Windo
ws, granted browser notifications surface through the system notification center.
## What it notifies
| DSH state | Notification title | Notes |

| `approval` | Approval request | The session is waiting for an approval decision. |
| `question` |

Question request | The session is waiting for a user choice or answer. |
| `plan-review` | Plan revi

ew | The session is waiting for plan confirmation. |
| `completed` | Completed | A top-level backgro

und session has finished. |
| `completed` on a subagent | Subagent completed | A subagent/background
child session has finished. |
## Highlights

- Browser-only; the host half is intentionally empty.
- Watches the live DSH session list and unifie

d session-status feed; no dependency on `dsh-web-ui-all`.
- Uses the public `sessions`, `uiSession`,

and `uiWorkspace` Client services; no DOM queries of core page structure.
- Opens the corresponding
session when a native notification or fallback toast is clicked; the toast also supports Enter and

Space. Window activation is subject to browser, desktop application, and OS policy.
- Responds to st
ore subscriptions without fixed-interval polling; relies on DSH to publish updates and replay pendin

g requests on reconnect.
- Uses native browser notifications first, with `requireInteraction: true`.

- Falls back to a larger right-bottom toast panel when native notifications fail.
- Supports multip

le stacked fallback toasts.
- Deduplicates unchanged requests by their opaque key and unread complet

ions by state; another request or a later completion can notify again.
- Does not treat idle histori
cal sessions as newly completed; the main-view session follows DSH's completion acknowledgement poli

cy.
- Keeps deduplication, timers, and toast cleanup independent across Client contexts and reloads.

- Labels completed subagents separately from completed top-level sessions.
- Unknown future pending
-interaction kinds are ignored safely until they have an explicit notification mapping.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
After installation, restart `dsh web` and reload the DSH Web GUI page. The browser may ask for notif
ication permission on first load. While permission is ungranted, the plugin immediately shows in-pag
e toast reminders, even if the permission prompt never settles. Native notification creation failure
s also fall back to toast.
### Desktop and Web profiles
DSH Desktop has its own `desktop` profile; installing the plugin into the `web` profile does not aut
omatically change Desktop. In DSH 0.2.1-alpha.1 and 0.2.2-alpha.2, their default directories are `~/
.dsh/profiles/desktop` and `~/.dsh/profiles/web`; a `DSH_HOME` set for the desktop process changes t
he root. Start Desktop at least once to initialize its profile, then fully quit Desktop and its Host
before using `dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<absolute-plugin-path>`. Preserve existing prof
ile backups and make sure the CLI and Desktop use the same user and DSH_HOME. Restart Desktop and ve
rify the startup log and served JavaScript.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Useful scripts:
- `pnpm test` — run all Vitest tests (build first after changing source). Includes the shipped bundl

e against the published DSH UiSession service, with fixture remote events; no provider API calls.
-

`pnpm test:notify` — run the core notification behavior tests.
- `pnpm typecheck` — run TypeScript t

ype checking.
- `pnpm build` — generate `lib/` artifacts.
- `pnpm watch` — rebuild the client bundle
during development.
[该节后续省略]
## Notes and limitations

- This plugin does not implement a settings UI yet.
- Notification delivery depends on browser permi

ssion and the operating system notification policy.
- Notification clicks require the originating pa
ge to remain alive; archived or unavailable sessions may not open. Window activation on Windows and

Linux browsers and desktop applications requires platform-specific testing.
- In one Windows 10 22H2
/ DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.5 test, clicking a question notification selected the source session, but a
minimized window did not restore automatically; the selected session was visible after manual restor

ation. Window activation depends on the host and OS and is not guaranteed.
- The same device run did
not complete approval, plan review, fallback toast, background completion, or reconnect regression;
Linux and browser window activation remain unverified on real devices. Automatic review that immedi

ately handles a request may leave no pending request to notify.
- Requires the DSH 0.2 unified statu
s API. DSH 0.1.2-alpha.2 is no longer supported by this release. The removed `SessionSummary.complet
ed` and `uiSession.pendingInteractions` fields are not used. Completion means DSH reports an unread

background stop; it does not certify that the task succeeded.
- Retained subagent rows in `sessions.
list.byId` are also observed, even when they are outside the Host catalog `ids`. Unknown metadata is

ignored until a label is available.
- Development types and real-service tests are pinned to 0.2.1-

alpha.1; other releases require compatibility validation.
- Notification text uses only the session'
s display label and fixed state wording; unrelated session fields are not included.
